name: What is a Junior ADU and how does it differ from a standard ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is a Junior ADU and how does it differ from a standard ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) is a living space created within the walls of an existing single-family home. Unlike a traditional ADU, a JADU must be carved out of an existing permitted space, such as a garage or a portion of the main house, and is typically smaller. It must include an efficiency kitchen, a bathroom, and a separate entrance. AKN Design Group focuses on maximizing the potential of your existing footprint for such transformations, ensuring the new space integrates seamlessly with your home's structure and aesthetics.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Junior ADU is a smaller, self-contained living space created within an existing home, featuring an efficiency kitchen and separate entrance.
